subject: Proposal: short-run pilot top-up and conversion path
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@clearcrest.ai>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Clare Holt <clare.holt@clearcrest.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Short pilot — request for 2-week top-up and conversion options

Kimberly,

Thanks again for running the demo last week — the engineering team at ClearCrest saw promising throughput on the summarization flow. We're coming up on the end of our 30-day pilot on Friday, and a couple of things popped up we want to run by you:  

- We spiked usage on Wednesday for a data ingestion window and burned through ~35% of the allocated tokens (attached usage report).
- Our product team wants a short 2-week extension (time-boxed) to validate the read/update loop under heavier concurrency, but we need clarity on cost and how that maps to conversion credits or a minimum commit if we move to a paid tier.

High-level asks: can Redwood provide a one-time top-up of pilot capacity (tokens) or add two calendar weeks to the pilot? If top-up, what is the exchange rate to committed spend (i.e., do top-up tokens count toward early conversion credits)? Also, we'll need a short SLA note on latency for the extended window — 95th percentile under our current test load.

Thanks,
Sanjay
VP of Product
ClearCrest AI

Attachments: pilot-usage-report.csv (CSV, 42KB)

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@clearcrest.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Jun 2025 08:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Short pilot — request for 2-week top-up and conversion options

Hi Sanjay — appreciate the note and the usage detail. Short answer: yes, we can accommodate a 2-week time-box extension or a one-off token top-up. Below are two structured options so your procurement and product teams can pick what fits best:  

Option A — 2-week time-box extension (no extra spend up front)
- Extension covers identical capacity/limits as your existing pilot.
- We require written acknowledgement that the extension is solely for evaluation (no SLA-backed uptime).
- If you convert to a paid contract within 30 days, we can apply a 25% credit of the incremental value of the extension toward the first-month committed spend.

Option B — Token top-up (applied immediately)
- One-time token bucket: 250K tokens at the pilot rate.
- If you convert within 30 days, top-up tokens are eligible for a 60% rebate (applied as credit) toward the committed monthly quota (not retroactive to usage prior to purchase).

Engineering/SLA note (95p latency): we can guarantee a best-effort 95th percentile on hosted tier for the extension window; for an SLA-backed 95p you'd need a short Dedicated evaluation (we can set up a dedicated pool for a week with a trial surcharge).

Next steps I propose:
1) Tell us whether you prefer Option A (time-box) or B (token top-up).
2) If Option B, we'll send an amendment and invoice (DocuSign link).
3) If Option A, we'll schedule a quick intake with Aditya for capacity checks and update the pilot config.

CC'd Marissa on conversion credits and Aditya on the engineering intake. Happy to hop on a 30-min call if helpful.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed-amendment-v1.pdf (PDF, 18KB)

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@clearcrest.ai>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Jun 2025 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Short pilot — request for 2-week top-up and conversion options

Sanjay — quick note on pricing mechanics and tradeoffs to consider when deciding:  

- Option A (time-box) is lowest friction for procurement, but the extension is not invoiced and therefore we only apply a partial conversion credit (25% of the extension's estimated value). That works well if you want more time for product validation without committing budget.
- Option B (token top-up) gives you a clearer runway and gives procurement a tangible invoice that can be rolled into a P.O. If you plan to convert to a committed monthly quota, Option B triggers a larger rebate (60%) which effectively reduces first-month committed spend.

A hybrid we sometimes use: sell a small token top-up (e.g., 100K tokens) + 2-week extension. That buys runway and buys down conversion economics. If that sounds interesting we can price a hybrid and include a line-item rebate schedule in the amendment.

Also, for the engineering team — Aditya, can you confirm capacity is OK for a 2-week extension under their current concurrency profile (see Sanjay's attached usage)?

Thanks,
Marissa
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

On capacity: see Aditya's note below in thread.

Cc: Clare Holt <clare.holt@clearcrest.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Jun 2025 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Short pilot — request for 2-week top-up and conversion options

Thanks Kimberly/Marissa — helpful framing. We're comfortable with a hybrid: 100K token top-up + a 2-week time-box extension. A few quick items before I sign the amendment:  

1) Can you confirm that the 100K top-up will be eligible for the 60% rebate toward our first-month committed quota if we convert within 30 days?
2) We'll need a one-paragraph note in the amendment clarifying that the time-box extension is evaluation-only (no uptime SLA) but Redwood will designate an engineering contact for prioritized support during the two weeks.
3) Requesting a single consolidated invoice (top-up + any administrative fee) we can route to procurement.

If you can confirm the above, I'll route the DocuSign and procurement will issue a PO. We're aiming to have the extension in place by Friday.

Best,
Sanjay
VP of Product, ClearCrest AI
